matters.title: WWTF West Secondary Clarifier Equipment Purchase
matters.text: Adopt a Resolution awarding the purchase of Walker Process Equipment brand secondary clarifier mechanism and associated equipment to MuniQuip, LLC of Roseville, CA in the amount of $539,798 for the West Secondary Clarifier Rehabilitation Project, with the finding that it is in the best interest of the City, and authorizing a procurement contingency of $110,202

ATTACHMENT 1
RESOLUTION NO. _________
RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF YUBA CITY AWARDING THE
PURCHASE OF A WALKER PROCESS EQUIPMENT SECONDARY CLARIFIER
MECHANISM AND ASSOCIATED EQUIPMENT TO MUNIQUIP, LLC OF ROSEVILLE, CA IN
THE AMOUNT OF $539,798 AND AUTHORIZING A PROCUREMENT CONTINGENCY OF
$110,202 FOR THE WEST SECONDARY CLARIFIER REHABILITATION PROJECT
WHEREAS, the 2020 Wastewater Master Plan identified rehabilitation and replacement
of aging wastewater treatment infrastructure, including secondary clarifier mechanisms, as a
priority condition-related improvement necessary to maintain reliable treatment operations and
regulatory compliance; and
WHEREAS, the Public Works Department Engineering Division has developed the West
Secondary Clarifier Rehabilitation Project to replace the existing clarifier mechanism and
associated components while preserving the existing concrete structure; and
WHEREAS, the City has determined that the most expedient and beneficial means by
which to facilitate the West Secondary Clarifier Rehabilitation Project is to procure long-lead
time clarifier equipment in advance of construction bidding; and
WHEREAS, the existing secondary clarifier mechanism was originally furnished by
Walker Process Equipment, and procurement of replacement equipment from the original
equipment manufacturer will ensure compatibility with the existing facility while minimizing
project costs, schedule impacts, and construction risks; and
WHEREAS, MuniQuip, LLC of Roseville, California is the authorized regional
representative for Walker Process Equipment; and
WHEREAS, the City has met the requirements to sole source the equipment pursuant to
Public Contract Code Section 3400(c) and City Purchasing Policies Section 8-8.4.2; and
WHEREAS, the negotiated price for the equipment is reasonable and consistent with
similar proprietary wastewater treatment equipment; and
WHEREAS, the City Council now desires to authorize the sole source purchase of
Walker Process Equipment brand secondary clarifier equipment from MuniQuip, LLC.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the City Council of Yuba City as follows:
1. The City Council finds that all of the facts set forth in the recitals above are true and
correct and incorporated herein.
2. The City Council finds that a sole source award is appropriate because Walker Process
Equipment is the original equipment manufacturer of the existing secondary clarifier
mechanism, the proposed equipment is uniquely suited for the City's existing
infrastructure and operational requirements, and the proposed negotiated price is
reasonable and consistent with similar proprietary wastewater treatment equipment.
Given this, the City Council finds that it is in the best interest of the City to make a sole
source award to MuniQuip, LLC.
3. The City Council of the City of Yuba City awards the purchase of Walker Process
Equipment brand secondary clarifier mechanism and associated equipment to
MuniQuip, LLC of Roseville, California in the amount of $539,798, inclusive of applicable
sales tax.
4. The City Council further authorizes a procurement contingency in the amount of
$110,202 (20.4%) and authorizes the Public Works Director to approve purchase
modifications, additional equipment components, manufacturer-requested refinements
identified during submittal review, startup and inspection services, delivery and freight
adjustments, and other procurement-related costs associated with acquisition of the
Walker Process Equipment secondary clarifier equipment.
5. The City Manager is authorized to execute all documents necessary to effectuate this
purchase.
The foregoing Resolution was duly and regularly introduced, passed, and adopted by the
City Council of the City of Yuba City at a regular meeting thereof held on the 7th day of July,
2026.

CITY OF YUBA CITY
STAFF REPORT
Date: July 7, 2026
To: Honorable Mayor & Members of the City Council;
From: Public Works Department
Presentation By: Joshua Wolffe, Public Works Director
Summary
Subject: WWTF West Secondary Clarifier Equipment Purchase
Recommendation: Adopt a Resolution awarding the purchase of Walker Process Equipment brand
secondary clarifier mechanism and associated equipment to MuniQuip, LLC of
Roseville, CA in the amount of $539,798 for the West Secondary Clarifier
Rehabilitation Project, with the finding that it is in the best interest of the City,
and authorizing a procurement contingency of $110,202
Fiscal Impact: $650,000.00 – Account No. 981116-65501 (Secondary Clarifier Improvement)
Purpose:
To maintain the City's Wastewater Treatment Facility (WWTF) operational effectiveness through
proactive rehabilitation and maintenance.
Strategic Focus Area:
This project addresses the City Council's Strategic Goal of improving vital wastewater infrastructure
through the construction of a priority rehabilitation project.
Background:
The City operates three secondary clarifiers at the WWTF that provide critical settling of biological
solids following aeration. The clarifier mechanisms were originally installed in 1976, 1983, and 1998
and have exceeded or are approaching their useful service life.
The West Secondary Clarifier, constructed in 1976, has significant age-related deterioration and the
mechanism sustained damage in the 1980s that was never fully repaired. While WWTF staff have
successfully operated the facility around this deficiency, replacement of the mechanism is necessary to
improve reliability and reduce operational risk.
The 2020 Wastewater Master Plan identified rehabilitation and replacement of aging wastewater
treatment infrastructure, including secondary clarifier mechanisms, as a priority condition-related
improvement.
Analysis:
Staff developed a project to replace the existing clarifier mechanism and associated components in the
West Secondary Clarifier while preserving the existing concrete structure. The anticipated procurement
includes 20-22 weeks for equipment submittal preparation and review, followed by 36-38 weeks for
manufacturing and delivery of the equipment. This presents challenges and inefficiencies with the
standard design-bid-build procurement.
Staff instead recommends a phased delivery approach whereby the City procures the long-lead time
clarifier equipment directly and then subsequently bids installation under a separate construction
contract. This approach reduces schedule risk and allows equipment fabrication to proceed
concurrently with final project design and bidding.
Sole Source Justification:
Staff evaluated potential manufacturers that could provide the necessary replacement equipment. The
existing secondary clarifier mechanisms were originally furnished by Walker Process Equipment. While
alternative clarifier manufacturers exist, utilizing equipment from a manufacturer other than Walker
Process Equipment would likely require modifications to the existing bridge structure, center pier, drive
assembly, rake arm geometry, and other appurtenances. These modifications would increase project
costs, extend design schedules, and introduce additional construction risks. Standardization of
equipment at the WWTF provides consistent parts, operator training, and streamlined maintenance
practices, reducing the need for stocking multiple spare inventories and simplifying long-term
operations. Walker Process Equipment mechanisms have also demonstrated proven reliability over
decades of service at this facility, and continuing with the same manufacturer minimizes performance
risk.
Staff recommends purchasing the clarifier replacement equipment directly from Walker Process
Equipment through their west coast vendor, MuniQuip, LLC of Roseville, CA under a sole source
procurement. Procurement from Walker Process provides the most cost-effective and
operationally/technically appropriate solution for replacement of the existing clarifier mechanism.
Additionally, this procurement meets the requirements for sole sourcing pursuant to Public Contract
Code Section 3400(c) and is consistent with City of Yuba City Purchasing Policy Section 8-8.4.2.
During fabrication of the equipment, staff will advertise for bids for the installation of the equipment.
Installation will be timed to occur upon delivery of the equipment to the City.
Fiscal Impact:
The total project cost, including equipment procurement, installation, coating, and associated
improvements, is estimated at approximately $2,000,000.
The Walker Process Equipment secondary clarifier equipment has been quoted at $498,658.54.
Applicable sales tax is estimated at approximately $41,139, resulting in a total equipment procurement
cost of approximately $539,798. Staff recommends a total authorization of $650,000, which includes
the equipment purchase, applicable sales tax, and a contingency of approximately $110,200 (20.4%) to
address potential tax adjustments, freight-related costs, manufacturer-requested modifications,
additional equipment components, startup and field service support, and other procurement-related
costs associated with specialized long-lead wastewater treatment equipment.
There are sufficient funds budgeted in Account No. 981116-65501 (Secondary Clarifier Improvement)
for this encumbrance, as well as the total estimated project cost for the West Secondary Clarifier
Rehabilitation Project. No general funds are allocated to this project.
Alternatives:
1. Defer replacement and take no action at this time while continuing to operate the existing clarifier.
This would expose the WWTF to reliability and operational risks.
2. Direct staff to seek bids from alternative equipment manufacturers. This would reduce equipment
standardization, require significant structural modifications to the clarifier basin and appurtenant
structures, and further delay corrective action of a longstanding operational deficiency.
Recommendation:
Adopt a Resolution awarding the purchase of Walker Process Equipment brand secondary clarifier
mechanism and associated equipment to MuniQuip, LLC of Roseville, CA in the amount of $539,798
for the West Secondary Clarifier Rehabilitation Project, with the finding that it is in the best interest of
the City, and authorizing a procurement contingency of $110,202.

Inc, of Fairfield, CA in the amount of $135,232.28 for the Conventional Filter Blower Upgrade Project, finding that the action is categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) and that the award is in the best interest of the City

ATTACHMENT 1
RESOLUTION NO. _________
RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF YUBA CITY FINDING THE ACTION
CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM CEQA (CEQA GUIDELINES §15301) AND AWARDING
THE PURCHASE OF A HOFFMAN AND LAMSON MODEL 815 ADOO CONVENTIONAL AIR
FILTER BLOWER SYSTEM TO MCKENNA ENGINEERING AND EQUIPMENT CO, INC. OF
FAIRFIELD, CA IN THE AMOUNT OF $135,232.28 FOR THE CONVENTIONAL FILTER
BLOWER UPGRADE PROJECT.
WHEREAS, the City of Yuba City (City) recognizes the need for ongoing maintenance
and improvements to maintain continuous and reliable operation of the Water Treatment Plant,
for the health and wellbeing of our customers and the environment; and
WHEREAS, the 2020 Water Master Plan identified the upgrade of the conventional air
blower equipment as a priority project, and
WHEREAS, the Public Works Department has developed a phased Filter Air Blower
Upgrade Project (project) to address the critical need in a cost-effective and efficient manner;
and
WHEREAS, the City desires the purchase of one (1) Hoffman and Lamson Model 815
ADOO air blower, one (1) 75-horsepower motor, and two (2) valves from McKenna Engineering
and Equipment Co, Inc. in accordance with the City’s Purchasing Policies and Procedures, as
the air blower and motor equipment is proprietary equipment uniquely suited for the City’s water
treatment plant infrastructure and solely available from said vendor; and
WHEREAS, the City has met the requirements to sole source the equipment pursuant to
Public Contract Code section 3400(c) and City Purchasing Policies section 9.3.1; and
WHEREAS, the negotiated prices for the equipment from McKenna Engineering and
Equipment are reasonable and on par with similar proprietary equipment in the water industry;
and
WHEREAS, the City Council now desires to authorize the sole source purchase of said
equipment from McKenna Engineering and Equipment.
NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Yuba City as
follows:
1. The City Council finds that all of the facts set forth in the recitals above are true and
correct and incorporated herein.
2. The City Council finds that a sole source award is appropriate based on the specialized
nature of the equipment and the City’s existing facilities and operational requirements.
McKenna Engineering and Equipment Co, Inc. is an authorized distributor and service
provider for Hoffman and Lamson centrifugal blower equipment and is able to furnish a
like-for-like addition of the existing air blower and motor at the Water Treatment Plant.
The City Council further finds that the negotiable pricing proposed by McKenna
Engineering and Equipment Co, Inc. is fair and reasonable and consistent with pricing
for similar proprietary equipment commonly used in the water and wastewater industry.
Based on these findings, the City Council determines that awarding this procurement
through a sole source process is in the best interest of the City. Accordingly, the City
Council of the City of Yuba City awards the purchase of one (1) Hoffman and Lamson
Model 815 ADOO air blower, one (1) 75-horsepower motor, and two (2) valves to
McKenna Engineering and Equipment Co, Inc. of Fairfield, CA, in the amount of
$135,232.28.
3. The City has performed a preliminary environmental assessment of the Conventional Air
Filter Blower Project, and the City Council has determined that it falls within the Class 1
Categorical Exemption set forth in section 15301(existing facilities) which exempts
repair, maintenance, or minor alteration of existing public facilities and mechanical
equipment, because the project involves replacement and upgrade of existing filter
blower equipment at an operating wastewater treatment facility with no expansion of
existing or former use. Furthermore, none of the exceptions to Categorical Exemptions
set forth in the CEQA Guidelines, section 15300.2 apply to this project. As such City
Council adopts a Class 1 Categorical Exemption per CEQA Guidelines section 15301 for
this project.
The foregoing Resolution was duly and regularly introduced, passed, and adopted by the
City Council of the City of Yuba City at a regular meeting thereof held on the 3rd day of
February, 2026.

CITY OF YUBA CITY
STAFF REPORT
Date: February 3, 2026
To: Honorable Mayor & Members of the City Council;
From: Public Works Department
Presentation By: Joshua Wolffe, Public Works Director
Summary
Subject: WTP Filter Blower Addition Project
Recommendation: Adopt a Resolution awarding the purchase of a Hoffman and Lamson model 815
ADOO Conventional Air Filter Blower System, to McKenna Engineering and
Equipment Co. Inc, of Fairfield, CA in the amount of $135,232.28 for the
Conventional Filter Blower Upgrade Project, finding that the action is
categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15301
(Class 1 – Existing Facilities) and that the award is in the best interest of the City
Fiscal Impact: $220,335.28 – Account No. 971227-65501 (Recurring WTP & Satellite Facility
Maintenance)
Purpose:
Facilitate continued reliable operation of the Water Treatment Plant’s (WTP) filtration system, by
upgrading current air blower equipment with a new additional unit and motor.
Council's Strategic Goal:
This project addresses the City Council's Strategic Goal of improving vital water Infrastructure through
the construction of a priority rehabilitation project.
Background:
The City’s Water Treatment Plant (WTP) has a treatment capacity of up to 36 million gallons per day
(MGD) and includes both conventional and membrane filtration systems. The conventional filtration
system, which treats up to 24 MGD, utilizes sand and anthracite media that require periodic
backwashing to remove accumulated solids. During the backwash process, compressed air is injected
through the filter media to scour and dislodge trapped particles.
The existing conventional filter air blower and motor have been in continuous service since 1999 and
have exceeded their typical useful life of 23 years. Failure of the equipment would significantly impact
the City’s ability to perform effective filter backwashing and maintain reliable treatment operations.
The 2020 Master Plan identified the lack of redundancy in the conventional filter air blower system as a
critical operational risk and recommended installation of a second blower to provide full system
redundancy. This improvement was designated as a priority project for completion within 1 to 5 years to
reduce risk of unplanned outages and maintain regulatory compliance.
Analysis:
Public Works Engineering Staff have developed a phased Filter Air Blower Upgrade Project (Project) to
address this critical need in a cost-effective and efficient manner.
Project Phases:
Public Works Engineering staff have developed a phased Conventional Filter Blower Upgrade Project
to address the need for redundancy in a cost-effective and operationally effective manner. The project
includes the following phases:
1. Procurement of a new air blower and motor
2. Construction of concrete equipment pad to house new blower system (Public Contract Code
sole source)
3. Electrical installation, control integration, and SCADA programming (Public Contract Code sole
source and City Public Works staff)
4. Equipment start-up and Commissioning
Staff is requesting approval to purchase one (1) Hoffman and Lamson Model 815 ADOO air blower,
one (1) 75-horsepower motor, and two (2) valves from McKenna Engineering and Equipment Co, Inc.
This equipment matches the existing blower system and was selected to maintain compatibility, ensure
long-term serviceability, minimize operational risk, and avoid the need for system modifications.
The City’s Purchasing Policy and Public Contract Code allow for sole-source procurement when
equipment must be compatible with existing infrastructure and when equivalent alternatives would
require significant redesign or operational changes. Based on these criteria, staff determined the
procurement of in-kind Hoffman and Lamson through McKenna Engineering and Equipment in the
City’s best interest. Pricing has been reviewed and is considered fair and reasonable based on current
market conditions. Due to the manufacturer’s estimated 16 to 19 weeks lead time, staff recommends
purchasing the blower equipment in advance of construction to avoid project delays. Installation,
electrical work, and SCADA integration will be performed under a separate construction phase, with
final startup and commissioning coordinated with the equipment supplier. This approach allows the City
to maintain schedule flexibility and reduce overall project risk while ensuring continuous, reliable WTP
operations.
Environmental:
Staff has performed a preliminary environmental assessment of Conventional Filter Blower Upgrade
project and has determined that it falls within the Class 1 Categorical Exemption set forth in CEQA
Guidelines, section 15301 (existing facilities) as this contract involves replacement of existing
equipment at an operating wastewater treatment facility with no expansion of capacity or change in use.
Furthermore, none of the exceptions to Categorical Exemptions set forth in the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, section 15300.2 apply to this project.
Fiscal Impact:
Staff estimates the total construction cost for the Conventional Filter Blower Upgrade Project to be
approximately $220,335.28, based on current market prices for equipment, installation, and associated
work. To account for price fluctuation, supply chain uncertainty, and manufacturing cost variability, a
20% contingency has been included.
Estimated Project cost, inclusive of contingency is approximately $220,335.28, summarized as follows:
Air blower equipment, Motor, and valves $135,232.28
Contingency (20%) $27,046.46
Installation and Concrete Pad $51,294.93
Electrical, Programming, & Start Up (5%) $6,761.61
Total Project Cost $220,335.28
There are sufficient funds in Account No. 971227-65501 (Recurring WTP & Satellite Facility
Maintenance) for this encumbrance, as well as the total construction cost for the Conventional Filter
Blower Project.
Alternatives:
Do not approve the purchase of the air blower and motor equipment. This option may negatively impact
WTP operations and water quality as the existing air blower and motor have exceeded their standard
service life’s and are at risk of failure.
Recommendation:
Adopt a Resolution awarding the purchase of a Hoffman and Lamson model 815 ADOO Conventional
Air Filter Blower System, to McKenna Engineering and Equipment Co. Inc, of Fairfield, CA in the
amount of $135,232.28 for the Conventional Filter Blower Upgrade Project, finding that the action is
categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines section 15301 (Class 1 – Existing
Facilities) and that the award is in the best interest of the City.

ATTACHMENT 1
RESOLUTION NO. _________
RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF YUBA CITY
AWARDING THE PURCHASE OF FOUR (4) BREDEL-BRAND PERISTALTIC PUMPS AND
TWO (2) CONTROL PANELS TO MISCO WATER OF PLEASANTON, CA IN THE AMOUNT
OF $90,000.00, AND THE PURCHASE OF ONE (1) MODEL GCDO-6 5HP LIME MIXER TO
CLEVELAND MIXER OF CLINTON, CT IN THE AMOUNT OF $17,000.00
WHEREAS, the City of Yuba City (City) recognizes the need for ongoing maintenance
and improvements to maintain continuous and reliable operation of the Water Treatment Plant,
for the health and wellbeing of our customers and the environment; and
WHEREAS, the 2020 Water Master Plan identified the replacement of the lime feed
system equipment as a priority project, and
WHEREAS, the Public Works Department has developed a multi-phase Lime Storage
and Feed Upgrade Project to construct these identified needs in a cost-effective and efficient
manner, beginning with the purchase of the proprietary Bredel-brand pumps, motors, and
control panels, and Cleveland-brand mixer and associated parts; and
WHEREAS, the City desires to purchase four (4) Bredel-brand peristaltic pumps, two (2)
control panels, and associated parts from Misco Water of Pleasanton CA, in accordance with
the City’s Purchasing Policies and Procedures, as the pumps are proprietary equipment
uniquely suited for the City’s water treatment plant infrastructure and solely available from said
vendor; and
WHEREAS, the City desires to purchase one (1) model GCDO-6 5HP mixer and
associated parts from Cleveland Mixer of Clinton, CT, in accordance with the City’s Purchasing
Policies and Procedures, as the mixer is proprietary equipment uniquely suited for the City’s
water treatment plant infrastructure and solely available from said vendor; and
WHEREAS, the City has met the requirements to sole source the equipment pursuant to
Public Contract Code section 3400(c) and City Purchasing Policies section 9.3.1; and
WHEREAS, the negotiated prices for the equipment from Misco Water and Cleveland
Mixer are reasonable and on par with similar proprietary equipment in the water industry; and
WHEREAS, the City Council now desires to authorize the sole source purchase of said
equipment from Misco Water and Cleveland Mixer.
NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Yuba City as
follows:
1. The City Council finds that all of the facts set forth in the recitals above are true and
correct and incorporated herein.
2. The City Council finds that a sole source award is appropriate on grounds including that
Misco Water is the sole authorized distributor of the desired type of pumps, that only
these pump types would be financially and practically feasible given the current
operating system, facilities, and performance needs, and that the proposed negotiated
prices for Misco Water’s equipment are reasonable and on par with similar proprietary
equipment in the water industry. Given this, the City Council finds that it is in the best
interest of the City to make a sole source award to Misco Water for four (4) Bredel-brand
peristaltic pumps, two (2) control panels and associated parts. As such, the City Council
of the City of Yuba City awards the purchase of four (4) Bredel-brand peristaltic pumps,
two (2) control panels and associated parts to Misco Water of Pleasanton, CA in the
amount of $90,000.00, including contingency.
3. The City Council finds that a sole source award is appropriate on grounds including that
Cleveland Mixer is the sole authorized distributor of the desired type of mixer, that only
this mixer would be financially and practically feasible given the current operating
system, facilities, and performance needs, and that the proposed negotiated price for
Cleveland Mixer’s equipment is reasonable and on par with similar proprietary
equipment in the water industry. Given this, the City Council finds that it is in the best
interest of the City to make a sole source award to Cleveland Mixer for one (1) Model
GCDO-6 5HP Mixer and associated parts. As such, the City Council of the City of Yuba
City awards the purchase of one (1) GCDO-6 5HP Mixer and associated parts to
Cleveland Mixer in the amount of $17,000.00, including sales tax, freight, and
contingency.
The foregoing Resolution was duly and regularly introduced, passed, and adopted by the
City Council of the City of Yuba City at a regular meeting thereof held on the 18th day of March,
2025.
